title: AppTaskPlan
description: The task_plan an app-studio mission produces — a DAG of work units grouped into waves. Extracted after the tutor genesis pilot's own plan.json passed its owner-approved plan gate (D066 build-then-extract). Its shape is not a free choice: every work unit carries a literal agent prompt and machine-checkable verify steps (a plan that is only a to-do list is a regression); ownership is tagged four ways because that is the cheapest honest signal for what no agent can do; and the two ordering signals are kept separate — hard `dependsOn` edges on units, soft `recommendedOrder` at wave level — because conflating them loses the difference between "cannot start" and "better later". Rolling wave: only the next wave is detailed, the rest are `outlineOnly`.

appName.description: Functional name (D002) of the app this plan builds.

generatedAt.description: When this round of planning produced the plan.

round.description: Which planning round this is. A rejected plan gate produces a new round, not an edit.

waves.description: The waves, in number order. May be empty only before planning has run.

problems.description: DERIVED. Everything structurally wrong with this plan, in plain words — unresolved or cyclic dependency edges, units missing what their mode actually needs, a detailed wave with no exit checklist. Recomputed at read time, never stored; an empty array means the plan validated.

wave.description: A sprint: one authorized batch of work, ending in an owner review.

goal.description: What this wave is for, in one sentence.

outlineOnly.description: True for waves that are outline-only. Rolling wave: detail comes later, and an outline-only wave legitimately carries no units and no checklist. A plan that details everything up front is fiction — it just doesn't know it yet.

canAuthorize.description: DERIVED: no open decisions and not outline-only. Note it does NOT read `deferredToDispatch` — that list never blocks.

openDecisions.description: Blocks authorization until empty — the confirm-before-agents rule. ONLY things a person must actually rule belong here. Kept strictly distinct from `deferredToDispatch`; see that field for the defect that distinction exists to prevent.

deferredToDispatch.description: Things resolved at dispatch time BY DESIGN, not by anyone's decision: migration numbers, ports, the exact contracts tag. These do NOT block authorization. The distinction was found by the tutor pilot: three of its wave-1 "open decisions" were the lazy-namespace discipline working exactly as intended — a plan must never write a literal migration number — and they failed the plan gate's own check for no good reason. With one field meaning "blocks authorization" and no field meaning "deliberately deferred", a planner has nowhere honest to record the second, so it files it under the first and the gate reads correct behaviour as an outstanding problem. Optional rather than required precisely because the plans that proved this shape predate the field; a producer that omits it is read as an empty list, never as an unknown.

checklist.description: What the owner attests at this wave's review. Positive assertions only, and NOT a restatement of the units' verify lines — units smoke-test themselves, while the wave gate attests something larger and typically includes the negative assertions no single unit would think to make.

recommendedOrder.description: Soft ordering, by unit title. Distinct from the units' hard `dependsOn` edges — this says "better later", not "cannot start".

workUnit.description: One dispatchable piece of work — a single agent session's worth.

id.description: Allocated, never improvised. Unique across the whole plan; `dependsOn` edges resolve against it.

title.description: On an owner unit the title IS the instruction — there is no agent to prompt.

mode.description: Who does this work. Required, never inferred: `owner` is the load-bearing member — it is how a plan stays honest about the parts no agent can do (creating accounts, testing on a real device, judging taste), keeping those visibly on the board until the owner closes them rather than letting them quietly evaporate. `advisory` units are notes to the reader: nothing is dispatched and nothing closes.

mark.description: DERIVED. The mode's legend symbol, for rendering only.

branch.description: The branch this unit's work lands on. Null for owner and advisory units.

dependsOn.description: Hard prerequisites, by unit id. THIS is the DAG. Edges resolve across the whole plan, not just this wave, and must not cycle.

parallelOk.description: True when this unit may run alongside its siblings.

diagnoseFirst.description: Questions the agent must investigate and report on BEFORE writing anything. If what it finds contradicts the task, it says so and stops — a task built on a wrong assumption is worse than no task.

lazyAllocations.description: Global namespaces this unit touches, resolved at dispatch and never written literally into the plan — literal numbers written ahead of time have already collided twice.

prompt.description: The literal instruction text for the unit. Load-bearing for `agent` and `assisted` modes — an agent cannot act on a title. May be empty on `owner` and `advisory` units.

verify.description: How this unit closes, and the only thing that closes it. Required, never optional: a unit with no pass condition is the one that silently stays open forever — which is why an OWNER unit needs verify steps even though it needs no prompt.

model.description: Model to dispatch this unit with, when the plan has an opinion. Null means the dispatcher's default.

workUnit.$comment: Everything that is actually dispatched and actually closes must carry at least one verify step. `advisory` is exempt because nothing is dispatched and nothing closes. Written as a bare if/then rather than wrapped in an allOf: the allOf form makes json-schema-to-typescript emit an intersection with an index signature, which silently drops the excess-property checking `additionalProperties: false` is here to give TypeScript consumers.

verifyStep.description: One concrete, externally checkable pass condition — either a command with an expected outcome, or a manual check a person runs. Never "make sure it works": a step whose pass condition cannot be stated is not a verification, it is a hope.

run.description: The command to run. Null on a manual step.

manual.description: The check a person performs. Null on a runnable step.

not.description: A step must have something to run or something a person checks. Stated as a negative rather than an anyOf of two required-shapes on purpose: the anyOf form makes every generator emit two variant classes and a union, which would push a modelling detail of this rule onto every consumer constructing a verify step.
